concepts.def: Protecting species, habitats and ecosystems from harm and restoring those already damaged.
Protected area established to conserve wildlife and landscape; UK has 15.
Breeding endangered species in zoos to boost numbers and reintroduce to the wild.
Restoring ecosystems by reintroducing keystone species (e.g., wolves to Yellowstone, beavers to UK).
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (1973) regulating wildlife trade.
Species whose role disproportionately affects the ecosystem (e.g., sea otters, wolves).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Conservation — a core area of GCSE Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Conservation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Conservation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which body regulates wildlife trade internationally?
options: IUCN
CITES
WWF
UNEP

mcqs.q: Reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone is an example of?
options: Captive breeding
Rewilding
Bioremediation
Selective breeding

mcqs.q: What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?
options: Because plants only use carbon.
Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Richness counts how many species exist; evenness measures how balanced their abundances are.
They are the same measurement.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
Environmental protection at all costs.
Stopping all development immediately.
Because plants only use carbon.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Because plants only use carbon.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
Stopping all development immediately.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
